top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B044) is a discovery and an explanatory framework together. Melitz (2003) is an identifiable origin that put selection into exporting and reallocation across firms into a tractable general-equilibrium model, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple is a separable extension. Its qualitative predictions have been tested in firm-level data across many countries for over twenty years. It is a later and distinct advance on the increasing-returns trade theory recognised in 2008. The citation should rest on the mechanism and not on the model-dependent welfare magnitudes. The credit boundary is imperfect, since Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, and arguably Redding, fall outside a two-name award, but a theory-centred citation states that boundary honestly. I rank P002 (Autor, Hanson, Katz) second. It is important and empirically credible, but the three-name cap excludes Dorn, the one-versus-two-discoveries question is unresolved, and the persistence of China-shock effects and shift-share identification are still debated. I rank P000 last because both substantive proposals describe mature, creditable achievements. I base this on the proposals' content and not on the six-versus-five support count.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. My frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited on P001 or P002. I have no documented tie to Helpman, Melitz, Autor, Hanson or Katz. My field, labour economics, is proximate to P002, and I disclose that as field proximity and not as evidence of merit. I joined the committee in 2023, the year of the Goldin prize. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
